question:
A single-phase inductive load consumes real power $P_1=2.0\,\text{kW}$ from a $220\,\text{V}$ (rms), $50\,\text{Hz}$ supply at power factor $\cos\phi=0.6$ (lagging). The same load sometimes operates at a reduced level where it consumes $P_2=1.0\,\text{kW}$ while maintaining the **same** power factor $0.6$ lagging.

An engineer wants to connect **one fixed capacitor permanently in parallel** with the load such that:
1) At $P_1$, the overall power factor becomes $0.9$ lagging.
2) At $P_2$, the overall power factor must **not become leading**; it must remain lagging or at most unity.

Evaluate whether a single fixed capacitor can satisfy both conditions. If possible, determine the suitable capacitance; if not, justify why.

options.A: A single fixed capacitor of about $112\,\mu\text{F}$ satisfies both conditions.
options.B: A single fixed capacitor of about $80\,\mu\text{F}$ satisfies both conditions.
options.C: It is **not possible** to satisfy both conditions using a single fixed capacitor; a **switched/step capacitor bank** is required (about $112\,\mu\text{F}$ needed at $P_1$, but $\le 88\,\mu\text{F}$ to avoid leading at $P_2$).
options.D: Both conditions can be met by connecting the capacitor in **series** with the load instead of in parallel.
